recipes.batch_note: Croutons, Burger Sauce, and Pickled Jalapeños batch Sunday. Night-of: roast potatoes + cook beef, ~25 min total.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: skip jalapeños or use minimal pickled jalapeños.

recipes.name: Barbecue Pulled Pork Tacos with Apple Cider Slaw
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, mixing bowl
instructions: Toss cabbage, carrots, and cilantro with Apple Cider Vinaigrette. Season with salt. Refrigerate until ready.
Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a large skillet. Working in batches, add tortillas and cook, flipping halfway, until soft and lightly fried, ~1 min. Transfer to kitchen towel or tortilla warmer.
In same skillet over medium heat, add Pulled Pork and Peach Barbecue Sauce. Cook, stirring, until heated through, ~8 min.
Divide pork between tortillas. Top with slaw and serve warm.
recipes.batch_note: Uses remaining pulled pork from Sunday batch. Slaw uses same ACV Vinaigrette as the grain bowls — make extra.

recipes.name: Barbecue Chicken Salad with Sesame Seed Croutons
recipes.equipment: Grill (or stovetop skillet), mixing bowls

ingredients.name: Pickling liquid (from Pickled Jalapeños and Shallots)

instructions: Season chicken with salt, rest 5 min. Pour over 1/3 cup Peach Barbecue Sauce, toss to coat. Marinate at room temp 20 min or refrigerated up to 1 hour.

Oil grill grates, preheat to medium-high. Shake excess marinade off chicken. Grill over direct heat, covered, ~8 min. Flip and cook until thermometer reads 165°F, 6–8 min more. Discard remaining marinade.
Rest chicken 5 min. Dice into bite-sized pieces. Toss with remaining 1/3 cup+ Peach Barbecue Sauce.
Whisk olive oil and pickling liquid together. Add romaine, cabbage, tomatoes, cilantro, cheddar, and farro. Toss to coat. Divide between two bowls.
Top with BBQ chicken, Pickled Jalapeños and Shallots, and Sesame Seed Croutons.
Note: Can cook chicken in a stovetop pan instead of grill — same timing, just don't cover it.
recipes.batch_note: Farro, croutons, and pickled jalapeños batch Sunday. Marinate chicken ahead if desired. Grill or pan-cook night-of.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: skip jalapeños on top or use lightly.
recipes.seasonal_note: Best on the grill in summer. Stovetop works fine but loses the char.

recipes.name: Cheesy California Burgers with White Cheddar
recipes.equipment: Large skillet

ingredients.name: Romaine leaves, broken into large pieces

instructions: Combine ground beef, 1/4 cup cheddar, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Divide into two patties.

Heat oil in large skillet over medium to medium-high. Add patties and cook undisturbed ~3 min. Flip and top each with 1/4 cup cheddar. Cook ~3 min more until thermometer reads 155°F (medium-well). Transfer to plate, tent with foil.
Toast brioche buns in same skillet.
Spread Burger Sauce on buns. Top with patty, avocado (Cameron only), Pickled Jalapeños and Shallots, and romaine leaves.
recipes.batch_note: Burger Sauce and Pickled Jalapeños batch Sunday. Night-of cook, ~25 min total.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron gets avocado. Austin is allergic to avocado — never add to his burger.

recipes.name: Bruschetta Chicken Bowls with Yukon Gold Potatoes & Fresh Mozzarella
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, air fryer, baking sheet, broiler

ingredients.name: Salt, black pepper, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, paprika
Baby Yukon Gold potatoes, sliced into rounds
Salt, pepper, garlic powder, Italian seasoning

instructions: BRUSCHETTA TOPPING FIRST: Mix all bruschetta ingredients together — diced Roma tomatoes, halved cherry tomatoes, fresh basil, olive oil, balsamic vinegar, minced garlic, salt and pepper. Stir well and refrigerate until ready to use. It improves as it sits.

POTATOES: Coat potato rounds in 1 tbsp avocado oil. Season generously with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and Italian seasoning. Air fry at 425°F for 35 minutes, flipping halfway through. They should be golden and crispy on the edges.

CHICKEN: Pound chicken breasts thin — about 1/2 inch thick. Drizzle 1 tbsp avocado oil over both sides and press in all seasonings (salt, pepper, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, paprika). Heat remaining 1 tbsp avocado oil in a large pan over medium-low. Cook chicken through (about 6-8 min per side depending on thickness). Remove to a cutting board and rest 5-10 minutes.

BROIL THE CHICKEN: Line a baking sheet with foil. Slice rested chicken and lay flat on the sheet. Sprinkle mozzarella evenly over the top. Broil on LOW for 5 minutes or until cheese is fully melted and beginning to bubble. Watch closely — it can burn fast.
BUILD BOWLS: Evenly portion potatoes into 5 meal prep containers. Top each with mozzarella-covered sliced chicken. Add 1/3 cup bruschetta topping over the chicken.
OPTIONAL FINISH: Drizzle with balsamic glaze for a restaurant-quality finish — highly recommended.
MEAL PREP NOTE: Cool completely before lidding and refrigerating. Keep bruschetta topping on the side if preferred — add day-of to keep it fresh and prevent the potatoes from getting soggy.
Austin: full portion. Cameron: slightly smaller portion (~4/5 serving) to hit her lunch targets.
recipes.batch_note: Full 5-serving batch. Make the bruschetta topping first so it has time to marinate. Potatoes in the air fryer while chicken cooks on the stove — runs parallel. Total active time is under 30 min once everything is going.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: serve ~4/5 of a full portion to hit her calorie target (~490 cal). No avocado needed here — the bruschetta topping provides all the brightness.
recipes.seasonal_note: Best in summer when Roma and cherry tomatoes are at peak. In spring, use hothouse cherry tomatoes and add extra balsamic to compensate for less sweetness.

recipes.name: Overnight Protein Oats
recipes.serving_note: Makes 1 jar. Batch 4 jars Austin + 4 jars Cameron Sunday night.
instructions: Add oats, protein powder, Greek yogurt, almond milk, almond butter, honey, and chia seeds to a mason jar or airtight container.
Stir vigorously until protein powder is fully incorporated — no dry clumps.
Seal and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours, up to 4 days).
Morning-of: top with granola and sliced strawberries. Eat cold.
recipes.batch_note: Batch 8 jars Sunday night — 4 for Austin (larger portion), 4 for Cameron (smaller). Label A and C. Grab and go each morning. Good through Thursday — make fresh batch Thursday night for Fri/Sat/Sun.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron gets smaller oat portion and less almond butter. Add sliced avocado on the side as a separate container if desired. She may want a splash of hot sauce on her avocado.
recipes.seasonal_note: Topped with fresh Pittsburgh strawberries — peak late May season.

recipes.name: Turkey & Zucchini Egg Scramble Wraps
recipes.serving_note: Makes 6 wraps. Batch Sunday — 3 for Austin, 3 for Cameron. Reheat in Breville 3-4 min.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add ground turkey, break apart, cook 5-6 min until browned and no pink remains. Season with paprika, cumin, red pepper flakes, salt, pepper.
Add diced zucchini and spring onions. Cook 3-4 min until zucchini is just tender.
Push turkey-veg to edges. Crack eggs and pour egg whites into center. Scramble gently, folding into the turkey mixture as eggs set — about 2-3 min. Don't overcook; residual heat finishes them.
Remove from heat. Adjust seasoning.
Warm tortillas in Breville or dry skillet 30 sec per side.
Divide filling across 6 tortillas. Top each with crumbled feta and a spoonful of tomatillo salsa. For Cameron's 3 wraps, add avocado slices.
Roll tightly (fold sides, then roll from bottom). Wrap each in foil or parchment.
Refrigerate. Reheat in Breville at 325°F for 3-4 min.
recipes.batch_note: Full batch (6 wraps) Sunday. Label Austin's and Cameron's separately — Cameron's get avocado. Consume within 4 days. Best days 1-3.
recipes.cameron_note: Add avocado slices inside wrap before rolling. Her wraps get slightly lighter red pepper. She can add hot sauce from the fridge.
recipes.seasonal_note: Zucchini is hitting its early summer stride in Pittsburgh — great texture in scrambles.

recipes.name: Greek Lamb Keftedes Bowl (Lunch)
recipes.serving_note: Assembly only — uses batch-cooked keftedes. Makes 1 bowl. Scale for 2.
instructions: Grab pre-portioned keftedes from fridge. Reheat in microwave 60-90 sec or eat room temp.
Layer rice/quinoa in bowl as base.
Arrange arugula, cucumber, cherry tomatoes around the base.
Place keftedes on top. Add feta crumbles.
Spoon tzatziki alongside. Squeeze lemon, drizzle olive oil, sprinkle oregano.
Cameron: add avocado slices.
Pack in meal prep container the night before if bringing to work.
recipes.batch_note: Keftedes and tzatziki made Sunday batch. Rice/quinoa from Sunday rice cooker batch. All components keep 4-5 days refrigerated.
recipes.cameron_note: Add 1/4 avocado sliced on top. Cameron gets 3 keftedes and slightly less grain.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh arugula and cherry tomatoes tie this to late spring Pittsburgh produce.

recipes.name: Sesame-Ginger Salmon & Cucumber Rice Bowl (Lunch)
recipes.serving_note: Uses leftover miso-glazed salmon from Tuesday dinner. Makes 1 bowl.
instructions: Flake leftover salmon into large pieces.
Layer rice in bowl as base. Arrange cucumber slices and edamame.
Place flaked salmon on top. Scatter spring onions and sesame seeds.
Drizzle sesame-ginger dressing and soy sauce.
Austin: add sriracha. Cameron: add avocado slices.
Prep in containers night-before for next day grab-and-go.
recipes.batch_note: Sesame-ginger dressing batched Sunday (makes enough for the week). Salmon from Tuesday dinner — portion out 2 servings each into labeled meal prep containers Tuesday night.
recipes.cameron_note: Add 1/4 avocado. No sriracha. Can add a splash of rice vinegar for brightness.
recipes.seasonal_note: Light, refreshing bowl perfect for late spring Pittsburgh heat.

recipes.name: Grilled Chicken & Zucchini Caprese Salad (Lunch)
recipes.serving_note: Uses batch-grilled chicken thighs. Makes 1 large salad. Scale for 2.

ingredients.name: batch chicken thigh, sliced (from Sunday Breville batch)
grilled/air-fried zucchini ribbons or rounds (from batch)

instructions: Slice batch chicken thighs. Arrange arugula as base in large bowl or container.
Layer zucchini, cherry tomatoes, torn mozzarella, and basil over greens.
Place sliced chicken on top.
Drizzle balsamic glaze and olive oil. Season with flaky salt, pepper, red pepper (Austin).
Cameron: add avocado. Keep dressing separate if packing ahead.
recipes.batch_note: Chicken batch cooked Sunday (Breville Smart Oven). Zucchini can be roasted alongside chicken batch. Pack containers without dressing; drizzle at lunch.
recipes.cameron_note: Add 1/4 avocado sliced on top. Her dressing ratio can be slightly more olive oil, less balsamic for a milder profile.
recipes.seasonal_note: Zucchini at its late spring peak. Cherry tomatoes starting their run. Caprese is the quintessential May flavor.

recipes.name: Smoked Pulled Pork Lettuce Wrap Bowl (Lunch)
recipes.serving_note: Uses smoked pulled pork shoulder leftovers. Makes 1 bowl.

ingredients.name: plain Greek yogurt (sub for sour cream)

instructions: Pull smoked pork from fridge. Reheat in microwave 60-90 sec with a splash of water or apple cider vinegar to keep moist.
Layer rice in bowl. Arrange butter lettuce cups on the side or around the bowl.
Pile pulled pork on rice. Top with corn salsa, pickled onions, Greek yogurt.
Squeeze lime, scatter cilantro. Drizzle BBQ sauce and sriracha (Austin).
Cameron: add avocado. To eat: fill lettuce cups for wraps, or eat as deconstructed bowl.
recipes.batch_note: Pork, corn salsa, and pickled onions all from Saturday batch. Sunday lunch is pure assembly — no cooking required.
recipes.cameron_note: Add 1/4 avocado. Skip sriracha. A little extra BBQ sauce is fine.
recipes.seasonal_note: Late spring corn starting in PA — fresh if available, frozen works great for salsa.

recipes.name: Greek Lamb Keftedes with Tzatziki & Tabbouleh
recipes.serving_note: Makes 24 keftedes (serves 6 dinners + lunches). Full batch Sunday.

ingredients.name: English cucumber, grated and squeezed dry

instructions: KEFTEDES: Combine lamb, feta, garlic, spring onions, mint, parsley, oregano, paprika, cumin, red pepper, salt, pepper, egg, and panko in large bowl. Mix until just combined — don't overwork.
Portion into 24 balls (~1.5 oz each). Flatten slightly to a thick disk shape.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high. Sear in batches, 3-4 min per side, until browned outside and just cooked through (160°F internal). Don't crowd the pan.
TZATZIKI: Grate cucumber, squeeze out all moisture in a clean towel. Mix with Greek yogurt, dill, grated garlic, 1.5 tbsp lemon juice, salt. Refrigerate.
TABBOULEH: Toss cooked quinoa with cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, parsley, mint, olive oil, remaining lemon juice, salt, pepper.
TO SERVE DINNER: Plate 5 keftedes (Austin) or 4 (Cameron) over a generous bed of tabbouleh. Spoon tzatziki alongside. Warm pita on the side.
Cameron: add avocado sliced alongside.
recipes.batch_note: Full 24-keftede batch Sunday. Tzatziki keeps 5 days. Tabbouleh keeps 4 days. Keftedes keep 5 days — use 5 each for Monday dinner (Austin), 4 (Cameron), then remainder become Mon/Tue lunch bowls.
recipes.cameron_note: 4 keftedes for dinner (vs Austin's 5). Add 1/2 avocado sliced alongside. Her tabbouleh portion is slightly smaller.
recipes.seasonal_note: Spring herbs — fresh mint and parsley — are at their best right now.

recipes.name: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Snap Peas & Sesame Rice
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4 (2 dinner servings + 2 leftover lunch servings each for Austin and Cameron). Cook 4 fillets total.
instructions: MARINADE: Whisk miso, mirin, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and ginger in a bowl. Place salmon skin-side up in a dish, pour marinade over flesh side. Marinate 30 min at room temp or up to 24 hr refrigerated.
Preheat Breville broil or set oven to broil high. Line a sheet pan with foil.
Place salmon skin-side down on lined pan. Broil 10-12 min until glaze is caramelized and salmon flakes at thickest part. Don't flip.

SNAP PEAS: While salmon broils, heat a skillet over high heat. Add snap peas with 1 tsp sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Stir-fry 2-3 min — keep snap and bright green. Finish with a splash of soy sauce.
Plate: jasmine rice drizzled with sesame oil, snap peas alongside, salmon fillet on top. Scatter sesame seeds and spring onions.
Austin: add sriracha. Cameron: add avocado slices.
Set aside 2 extra fillets (one per person) for Wednesday/Thursday lunches — store whole in containers, flake when assembling bowls.
recipes.batch_note: Cook 4 fillets at once Tuesday. 2 for Tuesday dinner, 2 reserved for Wed/Thu sesame-ginger rice bowl lunches. DO NOT flake the leftover fillets until assembly day.
recipes.cameron_note: Smaller rice portion. Add avocado each time. Mild naturally — no adjustments needed.
recipes.seasonal_note: Snap peas at their absolute peak in late May Pittsburgh. The bright crunch is the seasonal star here.

recipes.name: Carne Asada Tacos with Corn Pico de Gallo
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4. Makes 12 tacos total (3 per Austin dinner / 2.5 per Cameron dinner, with extra corn pico).
instructions: MARINADE: Combine lime juice, orange juice, garlic, chipotle, cumin, paprika, and olive oil. Coat steak. Marinate minimum 2 hours, up to overnight.

CORN PICO: Char corn in dry skillet or under broiler until golden. Combine with diced tomatoes, red onion, jalapeño (Austin portion), cilantro, lime juice, salt. Make a big batch — this carries through Saturday smoker and Sunday pulled pork bowl.
STEAK: Remove from marinade, pat dry. Grill on tabletop griddle (or cast iron skillet) over high heat 4-5 min per side for medium. Let rest 5-7 min — essential.
Slice steak against the grain into thin strips.
Warm corn tortillas directly on griddle, 30 sec per side until charred in spots.
BUILD TACOS: Layer steak, corn pico, cotija, Greek yogurt crema. Cameron: add avocado. Austin: extra jalapeño available.
Serve with lime wedges.
recipes.batch_note: Make a large batch of corn pico Wednesday evening — it keeps 4 days and appears in Saturday smoker sides and Sunday pulled pork bowl. Steak is cook-fresh Wednesday; leftovers can carry to a lunch if desired.
recipes.cameron_note: Use 1 chipotle pepper (not 2) for marinade split. Add avocado. No jalapeño in her pico. Greek yogurt crema is great here.
recipes.seasonal_note: Late May corn in Pittsburgh — sweet and charrable. The pico bridges the Mexican and BBQ meals this week.

recipes.name: Basil & Zucchini Pasta with Hot Italian Sausage
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4. Cook full batch — halve sausage portion for Cameron.
instructions: Boil pasta in heavily salted water. Cook 1 min shy of al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks: heat 1 tbsp olive oil in large skillet over medium-high. Add sausage, sear until browned and cooked through, 5-6 min. Remove to a plate.
Add remaining olive oil to pan. Add garlic, red pepper flakes — 30 sec. Add zucchini, cook 3-4 min until edges golden.
Add cherry tomatoes, cook 2-3 min until they burst and release juices.
Add sausage back. Add drained pasta. Toss with a splash of pasta water, add Parmesan. Toss vigorously to emulsify into a light sauce, adding pasta water as needed.
Remove from heat. Fold in torn fresh basil and lemon zest.
Plate and serve with more Parmesan. For Cameron: serve from the zucchini-tomato side of the pan with lighter sausage.
Cameron: add avocado slices on side.
recipes.batch_note: Cook-fresh Thursday night. Leftovers keep 3 days — great cold or reheated with a splash of water.
recipes.cameron_note: Use only 2 oz sausage in Cameron's portion (lighter serving). No extra red pepper. Add avocado on the side.
recipes.seasonal_note: Zucchini and fresh basil are the defining late-spring combination. Don't skip the lemon zest — it brightens the whole dish.

recipes.name: Thai Basil Pork Stir-Fry (Pad Kra Pao)
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4. Cook-fresh Friday. Austin gets extra sauce and chili.

ingredients.name: ground pork (or sub ground turkey for leaner)
Thai bird chilies or serrano, sliced

instructions: Make sauce: whisk fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil. Set aside.
Heat wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking. Add oil.
Add garlic and chilies — stir-fry 20-30 sec. Do not burn.
Add ground pork, breaking into fine crumbles. Cook 4-5 min until cooked through with some caramelized bits.
Add spring onions, toss 30 sec.
Pour in sauce, toss to coat. Add Thai basil leaves all at once — fold in quickly over 30 sec until wilted but still bright. The basil is the star.
Taste and adjust (more fish sauce for umami, more chili for heat).
Fry eggs separately in a bit of oil — runny yolk.
Serve stir-fry over jasmine rice topped with fried egg, lime wedge. Austin gets extra chili on the side.
Cameron: add avocado and use just 1 mild chili in her portion.
recipes.batch_note: Cook-fresh Friday. Fast enough at 22 min to make on a weeknight. Leftovers taste even better day 2.
recipes.cameron_note: Use 1 mild serrano for Cameron's portion. Add avocado on side. The oyster sauce gives great umami without needing high heat.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh Thai basil is the non-negotiable here. If needed, add some Italian basil to supplement — flavor is slightly different but works.

recipes.name: Smoked Pulled Pork Shoulder
recipes.cook: 10-12 hr low and slow on smoker
recipes.serving_note: One 8-10 lb pork shoulder feeds 10-12 servings. Covers Saturday dinner + Sunday lunch for both + leftovers.

ingredients.name: apple wood or cherry wood chips
corn pico de gallo (from Wednesday batch)

instructions: FRIDAY NIGHT — DRY RUB: Coat pork shoulder all over with yellow mustard (this helps the rub adhere, won't taste mustardy). Combine brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, cayenne, black pepper, and salt. Rub thoroughly into every surface. Wrap in plastic, refrigerate overnight.
SATURDAY MORNING (6am): Fire up smoker to 225-250°F. Add apple wood chips (or cherry for a sweeter smoke).
Place pork shoulder fat-side up on smoker grate. Insert probe thermometer if you have one.
Smoke 8-10 hours, maintaining 225-250°F. Every 2 hours, spritz with apple cider vinegar to keep bark moist.
At 165°F internal: wrap tightly in butcher paper or foil. Return to smoker.
Continue until internal temp reaches 200-205°F — this is the pull temp. The bone should wiggle freely.
REST minimum 1 hour wrapped in a towel in a cooler. This is not optional.
PULL: Unwrap, remove bone. Use bear claws or two forks to pull into long strands. Season with remaining rub + apple cider vinegar splash.
SATURDAY DINNER: Serve on brioche buns with corn pico, pickled onions, BBQ sauce. Cameron gets avocado.
COLESLAW: For a no-cabbage version: shred kohlrabi, broccoli slaw mix, or just use thinly sliced snap peas + carrots. Toss with Greek yogurt, apple cider vinegar, honey, salt. Refreshing and crunchy.
recipes.batch_note: One big shoulder covers 2 meals for both Austin and Cameron. Saturday = dinner. Portion Sunday lunch amounts into containers Saturday night. Remaining pork freezes beautifully vacuum-sealed.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron gets same pulled pork — just smaller portion. Add avocado to her bun/bowl. Her coleslaw same recipe, slightly smaller side.
recipes.seasonal_note: Smoker season is fully open in Pittsburgh May. Apple wood is classic for pork — subtle sweetness that doesn't overpower.

recipes.name: Za'atar Shrimp with Herb Couscous & Lemon Tahini
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4. Cook-fresh Sunday. Light, bright season-closer for the week.

ingredients.name: large shrimp, peeled and deveined (21-25 count)

instructions: MARINADE: Toss shrimp with za'atar, 1.5 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, half the garlic, red pepper flakes, salt. Let sit 10-15 min.

COUSCOUS: Pour boiling chicken broth over dry couscous in a bowl, cover tight with plastic wrap, let steam 5 min. Fluff with fork. Toss with remaining olive oil, half the lemon juice, parsley, mint, cherry tomatoes, cucumber. Season with salt and pepper.
TAHINI SAUCE: Whisk tahini, remaining lemon juice, remaining garlic, honey, salt, and enough water to reach a drizzle consistency.
SHRIMP: Heat skillet or grill pan over high heat. Add shrimp in single layer, cook 2 min per side — pink, curled, with a little char on the edges. Don't overcook. Work in batches.
PLATE: Mound herb couscous, pile shrimp on top, drizzle tahini sauce. Garnish with spring onions and lemon wedge.
Cameron: add avocado alongside. Austin: add extra red pepper or harissa on the side.
recipes.batch_note: Cook-fresh Sunday night. Relatively quick — couscous takes 5 min, shrimp 4-6 min. Herb couscous can be pre-made and refrigerated; dress with olive oil to revive.
recipes.cameron_note: Add 1/2 avocado sliced. She'll love the tahini sauce — rich and bright. Mild spice level is perfect for her.
recipes.seasonal_note: Za'atar and fresh herbs signal the Mediterranean spirit of spring. Cherry tomatoes and cucumber are at their early-summer prime.

recipes.name: Turkey & Spinach Egg Scramble Wraps
recipes.serving_note: Makes 6 wraps — batch Sunday. 3 Austin / 3 Cameron. Reheat Breville 325F 3-4 min.
instructions: Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium-high. Add turkey, break apart, cook 5-6 min until browned. Season with paprika, cumin, red pepper, salt, pepper.
Add spring onions and garlic — 30 sec. Add spinach and stir until wilted, about 1-2 min.
Push turkey-spinach to edges. Pour eggs and egg whites into center. Scramble gently, folding into turkey mixture as they set — 2-3 min. Pull off heat while still slightly soft.
Warm tortillas in dry skillet or Breville 30 sec per side.
Divide filling across 6 tortillas. Top with feta and spoonful of tomatillo salsa. Cameron's 3 wraps: add avocado slice.
Roll tightly, wrap each in foil. Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat Breville 325F 3-4 min.
recipes.batch_note: Full 6-wrap batch Sunday. Label A vs. C. Cameron's wraps get avocado inside — mark clearly. Consume within 4 days.
recipes.cameron_note: Avocado slice inside wrap before rolling. Mark her foil wraps AVO so there's no mix-up.
recipes.seasonal_note: Baby spinach from this week's fresh supply — use it now before it wilts.

recipes.name: Arugula & Prosciutto Orzo Bowl
recipes.serving_note: Batch orzo + dressing Sunday. Assemble daily. Covers Mon/Tue/Wed lunches for both.
instructions: BATCH SUNDAY: Cook orzo per package directions. Drain, rinse with cold water, toss with 1 tbsp olive oil. Refrigerate.
DRESSING: Whisk shallot + lemon juice + Dijon + remaining olive oil + salt + pepper. Store in jar — keeps a week.
DAILY ASSEMBLY: Scoop orzo into bowl. Add arugula, cherry tomatoes, garbanzo beans, torn prosciutto, feta. Drizzle dressing. Toss.
Austin: add red pepper flakes. Cameron: add 1/4 avocado.
Pack in meal prep container with dressing on the side if bringing to work.
recipes.batch_note: Orzo + dressing batched Sunday covers Mon/Tue/Wed. Keep components separate — assemble fresh daily so arugula stays crisp.
recipes.cameron_note: Add 1/4 avocado. Her portion slightly less orzo + garbanzo. Same dressing.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh arugula from this week's haul — use it first before it wilts.

recipes.name: Pesto Chicken & Spinach Pasta
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4. Batch chicken in Breville Sunday, finish pasta Monday night in 15 min.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.qty: 2.5 lbs (full batch — saves rest for smoker)

ingredients.name: dry pasta (spaghetti, rigatoni, or whatever's open)

instructions: NOTE: If batch-cooking chicken Sunday in Breville, slice it for this dish Monday night. Otherwise, cook chicken separately: season with salt + pepper + garlic, bake at 400F 20-22 min until 165F.
Boil pasta in heavily salted water. Cook 1 min shy of al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.
Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium. Add garlic 30 sec. Add cherry tomatoes — cook 2 min until they soften.
Add sliced/shredded chicken. Add drained pasta. Add pesto + splash of pasta water. Toss vigorously.
Add spinach in handfuls, folding in until wilted. Add lemon zest. Season.
Plate, top with Parmesan and red pepper flakes (Austin). Cameron: add avocado alongside.
Leftovers keep 3 days — reheat with a splash of water.
recipes.batch_note: If chicken was batch-cooked Sunday, Monday dinner is 15 min total — just cook pasta and assemble. The pesto does the heavy lifting.
recipes.cameron_note: Smaller pasta portion. Add avocado on the side. Extra pesto is encouraged for her.
recipes.seasonal_note: Baby spinach from this week's fresh supply — perfect wilted into pasta.

recipes.name: Ginger-Soy Glazed Tilapia with Snow Peas & Brown Rice
recipes.serving_note: Serves 2 (1 lb tilapia). Cook-fresh Tuesday. Save 1 lb for Sunday Moroccan dinner.
instructions: GLAZE: Whisk soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, ginger, garlic, and rice vinegar.
Pat tilapia dry. Heat nonstick skillet over medium-high with a thin film of oil.
Cook tilapia 3-4 min per side until opaque and flakes easily. In last 2 min, spoon glaze over fish. It will caramelize quickly — watch the heat.
SNOW PEAS: In same pan (or alongside), stir-fry snow peas over high heat 2-3 min with a splash of soy sauce. Keep bright green and crunchy.
Plate rice, arrange snow peas, place tilapia on top. Drizzle remaining glaze. Scatter sesame seeds and spring onions.
Austin: add sriracha. Cameron: add avocado.
recipes.batch_note: Cook only 1 lb (2 fillets) Tuesday — save the second pound in the fridge for Sunday's Moroccan tilapia. Don't freeze and re-thaw.
recipes.cameron_note: Mild naturally. Add avocado alongside. Can skip sesame oil if she finds it overpowering.
recipes.seasonal_note: Snow peas from this week's fresh haul — cook them this week before they soften.

recipes.name: Chipotle Ground Turkey Taco Bowls
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4. Cook-fresh Wednesday. Uses pantry staples + freezer street corn.

ingredients.name: cooked brown rice or white rice

instructions: Heat skillet over medium-high. Cook turkey, breaking apart, until browned 5-6 min. Drain any excess fat.
Add garlic + chipotle + cumin + paprika + chili powder. Stir 1 min.
Add black beans + frozen street corn. Cook 3-4 min until corn is heated and beans are warm. Squeeze in lime juice.
Taste — adjust salt and heat.
BUILD BOWL: Rice base → turkey-bean-corn mixture → Greek yogurt crema → tomatillo salsa → feta → spring onions → cilantro.
Austin: full chipotle, extra hot sauce. Cameron: 1 pepper, add avocado.
recipes.batch_note: Cook-fresh Wednesday. Ground turkey is fresh (use this week!). Make a full batch — enough for 4 servings. Leftovers keep 4 days if needed for Thursday lunch.
recipes.cameron_note: 1 chipotle pepper (not 2). Greek yogurt crema cuts the heat nicely. Add avocado.
recipes.seasonal_note: Street corn from freezer — no need to buy fresh this week.

recipes.name: Lamb Keftedes with Pearl Couscous, Tahini & Garbanzo
recipes.serving_note: Makes 20 keftedes (batch Sunday). Serves 4 dinners (5 Austin / 4 Cameron) + Thu/Fri lunches.
instructions: KEFTEDES: Combine lamb, feta, garlic, spring onions, mint, parsley, oregano, cumin, paprika, egg, panko, salt, pepper. Mix until just combined.
Roll into 20 pieces (~1.5 oz each). Flatten slightly.
Heat cast iron or skillet over medium-high. Add oil. Sear keftedes 3-4 min per side until browned and cooked through (160F). Work in batches — don't crowd.
TAHINI SAUCE: Whisk tahini + lemon juice + grated garlic + salt + enough water to reach drizzle consistency.
PLATE: Spinach or arugula base. Pearl couscous. Garbanzo beans. 5 keftedes (Austin) / 4 (Cameron). Cherry tomatoes. Tahini drizzle.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado.
recipes.batch_note: Full 20-keftede batch Sunday. Thu dinner: 5 each (Austin), 4 each (Cameron). Remaining goes into Thu/Fri lunch bowls. Tahini sauce keeps 5 days.
recipes.cameron_note: 4 keftedes for dinner. Add avocado. Extra tahini drizzle — she'll love it.
recipes.seasonal_note: The mint and parsley are essential here — fresh herbs elevate the lamb significantly.

recipes.name: Lamb Keftedes Couscous Bowl (Lunch)
recipes.serving_note: Assembly only — uses batch keftedes from Sunday. Covers Thu/Fri lunches.
instructions: Reheat keftedes in microwave 60-90 sec.
Layer couscous, spinach/arugula, garbanzo, cherry tomatoes in bowl or container.
Place keftedes on top. Drizzle tahini sauce. Squeeze lemon.
Cameron: add avocado.
recipes.batch_note: All components from Sunday batch. Pure assembly. Pack night-before in containers.
recipes.cameron_note: 3 keftedes. Add avocado. Extra tahini.
recipes.seasonal_note: Uses fresh greens from this week's haul.

recipes.name: Thai Basil Beef Stir-Fry (Pad Kra Pao — Beef Version)
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4. Cook-fresh Friday. Beef fondue slices = pre-thinly-sliced — perfect for stir-fry.
instructions: SAUCE: Whisk fish sauce + oyster sauce + soy sauce + sesame oil. Set aside.
Heat wok or large skillet until smoking. Add vegetable oil.
Add garlic + chilies — 20 sec. Watch it.
Add beef slices in a single layer as best you can. Let sear 1-2 min undisturbed, then stir-fry 1-2 min more until cooked through.
Add snow peas/pepper blend + celery + spring onions — toss 1-2 min.
Pour sauce over. Toss. Add Thai basil all at once — fold in over 30 sec until wilted but bright.
Taste: more fish sauce for umami, more chili for heat.
Fry eggs separately in a little oil — runny yolk traditional.
Serve over rice, topped with fried egg, lime wedge. Austin: full chili load. Cameron: 1 serrano, add avocado.
recipes.batch_note: Cook-fresh Friday — 22 min start to finish. Beef fondue slices are already thin-cut, which makes this weeknight-viable.
recipes.cameron_note: 1 serrano. Add avocado. The oyster sauce provides enough depth at mild heat.
recipes.seasonal_note: Thai basil is the essential non-negotiable here — must buy fresh.

recipes.name: Garbanzo, Tahini & Spinach Bowl (Pantry Lunch)
recipes.serving_note: Pure pantry assembly. Saturday lunch while smoker runs. No cooking required.
instructions: Whisk tahini + lemon juice + grated garlic + water + cumin + salt until smooth drizzle consistency.
Layer spinach in bowl. Top with couscous, garbanzo, cherry tomatoes, feta.
Drizzle tahini sauce and olive oil. Toss gently.
Austin: red pepper flakes. Cameron: add avocado.
Eat while the smoker does its thing.
recipes.batch_note: Entire lunch from pantry — no shopping or cooking required. Uses garbanzo, couscous batch, tahini, and remaining produce.
recipes.cameron_note: Add avocado. More tahini is always right for her.
recipes.seasonal_note: Simple and light — the smoker is the star of Saturday, not lunch.

recipes.name: Smoked Chicken Thighs with Mexican Street Corn & Garbanzo Salad
recipes.serving_note: 2.5 lbs chicken thighs. Covers Saturday dinner + Sunday lunch for both.
instructions: FRIDAY NIGHT: Mix dry rub (paprika, garlic powder, brown sugar, cayenne, salt, pepper). Pat chicken dry, rub all over including under skin. Refrigerate overnight.
SATURDAY: Fire smoker to 275F. Apple or cherry wood.
Smoke chicken thighs until 175F internal — about 3-4 hours. Skin will be deep mahogany.
Rest 15 min before serving.
STREET CORN SALAD: Heat frozen corn in skillet with a dry pan until charred in spots. Combine with Greek yogurt, lime juice, chili powder, feta, spring onions. Season.
GARBANZO: Toss drained garbanzo with olive oil, lemon, cumin, salt, spring onions.
PLATE: 2-3 thighs per person + street corn + garbanzo. Drizzle BBQ sauce. Cameron: add avocado.
SAVE: Pull remaining thighs Saturday evening — shred for Sunday lunch bowls.
recipes.batch_note: Saturday dinner covers 2-3 thighs each. Pull remaining chicken Saturday evening into shreds — refrigerate for Sunday smoked chicken wrap bowls.
recipes.cameron_note: Same chicken. Add avocado on corn side. She can skip the cayenne heat in the rub next time if it's too much.
recipes.seasonal_note: Late May Pittsburgh — smoker season is fully open. Chicken thighs take only 3-4 hours at 275F.

recipes.name: Smoked Chicken & Spinach Wrap Bowl (Sunday Lunch)
recipes.serving_note: Assembly only — uses Saturday's smoked chicken. Sunday lunch.

ingredients.name: cooked brown rice or pearl couscous

instructions: Pull smoked chicken from fridge. Microwave 60 sec with a splash of water.
Bowl: grain base + spinach + smoked chicken + tomatillo salsa + Greek yogurt + spring onions + lime.
Cameron: add avocado. Austin: extra tomatillo salsa or hot sauce.
recipes.batch_note: Saturday evening: pull all remaining smoked chicken and portion into 2 Sunday lunch containers. No prep required Sunday — grab and go.
recipes.cameron_note: Add avocado. The tomatillo salsa is already in the pantry — she'll love it over the chicken.
recipes.seasonal_note: Uses up the remaining baby spinach before it turns.

recipes.name: Moroccan-Spiced Tilapia with Pearl Couscous & Tahini
recipes.serving_note: Serves 2 (uses remaining 1 lb tilapia from Tuesday's purchase). Cook-fresh Sunday.

ingredients.name: tilapia fillets (remaining 1 lb from Tuesday thaw)
fresh parsley or mint (if any left)

instructions: SPICE RUB: Mix cumin, paprika, garlic powder, cinnamon, red pepper, salt. Coat both sides of tilapia.
TAHINI SAUCE: Whisk tahini + lemon juice + water + salt until smooth drizzle consistency.
Heat skillet or Breville broil over medium-high. Add olive oil. Cook tilapia 3-4 min per side until opaque and slightly crisp on edges. Squeeze lemon over in last 30 sec.
COUSCOUS BASE: Toss cooked pearl couscous with garbanzo, spinach, cherry tomatoes, olive oil, lemon zest, salt.
PLATE: Couscous base → tilapia fillet → tahini drizzle → fresh herbs + lemon zest.
Cameron: add avocado alongside. Austin: extra red pepper or harissa if available.
recipes.batch_note: This is the week's closer — Sunday dinner using the last pound of tilapia. Pearl couscous from Sunday batch. No extra shopping needed.
recipes.cameron_note: Add avocado. Extra tahini. This is a mild, elegant finish to the week — perfect for her.
recipes.seasonal_note: Uses up remaining produce: spinach, cherry tomatoes, citrus. Clean-out-the-fridge energy with restaurant-quality flavor.
equipment: skillet or Breville Smart Oven Pro

recipes.name: Berry Protein Overnight Oats
instructions: In each of 4 jars or containers: combine 1/2 cup rolled oats, 1 scoop vanilla protein powder, 1/3 cup Greek yogurt, 2/3 cup almond milk, and 1 tbsp chia seeds.
Stir well to combine — make sure protein powder is fully mixed in (no clumps).
Seal and refrigerate overnight (minimum 6 hours, up to 5 days).
Morning-of: pull from fridge 15-20 min before eating. Top with sliced strawberries, blueberries, and 1 tbsp almond butter (Austin) or 1 tbsp coconut flakes (Cameron).
Austin gets a slightly larger base portion for his calorie target; Cameron keeps standard portions.
recipes.batch_note: Prep all 4 jars Saturday night. Keeps 5 days refrigerated. Top fresh each morning.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron uses coconut flakes instead of almond butter; smaller base portion (2/3 cup almond milk, slightly less yogurt).
recipes.seasonal_note: Peak strawberry + blueberry season in Pittsburgh — use the freshest berries you can find.
recipes.equipment: Mason jars or meal prep containers

recipes.name: Zucchini-Turkey Sausage Egg Bites
recipes.serving_note: Makes 12 bites (Tue/Thu/Sat breakfasts — Austin 4, Cameron 3 per day)

macro_strings.cameron: 410 cal | 33g P | 19g F | 9g C (3 bites + avocado)

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin well.
Shred zucchini on the large holes of a box grater. Squeeze in a clean kitchen towel to remove excess moisture — this is critical or the bites will be watery.
Whisk egg whites and whole eggs in a large bowl. Add turkey sausage crumbles, squeezed zucchini, spring onions, feta, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper.
Fill each muffin cup about 3/4 full.
Bake 20-22 minutes until puffed and set in the center. A toothpick should come out clean.
Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then remove to a wire rack. Store airtight up to 5 days.
Reheat: microwave 45-60 seconds or Breville at 325°F for 5 min.
recipes.batch_note: Prep Sunday during batch cook. Austin eats 4 bites per morning, Cameron 3 bites + avocado side.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron adds 1/4 sliced avocado on the side for healthy fats and creaminess.
recipes.seasonal_note: Zucchini is peaking — use it up! Spring onions add brightness.
recipes.equipment: 12-cup muffin tin, box grater

recipes.name: Mediterranean Chicken & Cucumber Grain Bowl
instructions: Divide quinoa evenly into 4 meal prep containers.
Top each with sliced harissa chicken (Austin gets 6 oz, Cameron gets 4 oz).
Add diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, olives, and feta.
Garnish with fresh parsley. Keep dressing in small side containers — dress day-of.
Cameron: add 1/4 sliced avocado fresh each day + extra feta crumble.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble 4 bowls Sunday. Dressing on the side. Keeps 4 days.
recipes.cameron_note: + 1/4 avocado sliced fresh daily, extra feta crumble.
recipes.seasonal_note: Cucumber and cherry tomatoes at their summer best.
recipes.equipment: Meal prep containers

recipes.name: Spicy Gochujang Chicken Lettuce Wraps
instructions: Quick-pickle cucumbers: slice thin, toss with rice vinegar + pinch sugar + pinch salt; let sit 15 min while assembling.
Warm shredded gochujang chicken and toss with additional gochujang glaze.
Portion into containers: chicken + rice + pickled cucumbers + julienned carrots in main compartment; butter lettuce leaves in separate bag/container.
Day-of: spoon chicken and rice into lettuce cups, top with pickled cucumber, carrots, sesame seeds, scallions.
Austin: extra gochujang drizzle. Cameron: use less glaze, add avocado.
recipes.batch_note: Prep 4 containers Sunday. Keep lettuce separate. Assemble at lunch.
recipes.cameron_note: + 1/4 avocado in wraps, use lighter gochujang drizzle.
recipes.seasonal_note: Crisp butter lettuce + fresh cucumbers = perfect summer wrap vehicle.
recipes.equipment: Meal prep containers, small bags for lettuce

recipes.name: Italian Zucchini & Chicken Pesto Pasta Salad
instructions: Cook pasta per package to al dente. Drain, rinse with cold water, toss with 1 tsp olive oil.
Sauté diced zucchini in 1 tbsp olive oil over high heat 3-4 min until lightly charred but still crisp. Season with salt + pepper. Cool.
Toss cooled pasta with pesto, diced chicken, sautéed zucchini, cherry tomatoes, mozzarella pearls, lemon juice.
Portion into 4 containers. Top with fresh basil day-of.
Austin gets 6 oz chicken per serving; Cameron gets 4 oz.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble Sunday. Keeps 4 days. Add extra pesto drizzle day-of if dry.
recipes.cameron_note: + 1/4 avocado sliced fresh, extra pesto drizzle.
recipes.seasonal_note: Peak zucchini + fresh basil + cherry tomatoes = summer Italian perfection.
recipes.equipment: Large pot, large skillet

recipes.name: Smoked Pork Tenderloin Grain Bowl
instructions: Divide grain base into 2 bowls.
Top with sliced smoked pork (Austin 6 oz, Cameron 4 oz), arugula, cucumber, tomatoes, pickled red onion.
Drizzle with tzatziki on one side and cherry BBQ glaze on the other — the sweet-smoky + tangy combo is the move.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado, extra tzatziki.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble fresh Sunday from Saturday smoker leftovers.
recipes.cameron_note: + 1/4 avocado, extra tzatziki drizzle.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh arugula + cherry BBQ = summer fusion.
recipes.equipment: None — assembly only

recipes.name: Harissa Chicken Thighs with Roasted Zucchini & Couscous
instructions: Marinate chicken thighs with harissa paste, 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper for at least 15 min (or use batch-prepped harissa chicken from Sunday).
Toss zucchini half-moons with 1 tbsp olive oil + salt + pepper. Roast at 425°F for 15 min until lightly charred.
While zucchini roasts, cook chicken thighs in a hot skillet over medium-high, 5-6 min per side until cooked through and charred. OR use batch-prepped harissa chicken (warm in skillet 3 min).
Prepare couscous: bring chicken broth to a boil, add couscous + lemon zest, cover, remove from heat, let steam 5 min, fluff with a fork.
Plate: couscous base, sliced harissa chicken, roasted zucchini. Garnish with mint, parsley, a dollop of Greek yogurt, extra lemon squeeze.
Austin: 8 oz chicken. Cameron: 5 oz chicken, slightly more couscous.
recipes.batch_note: Can use batch-prepped harissa chicken from Sunday for faster weeknight assembly.
recipes.cameron_note: Smaller chicken portion; extra couscous and a generous yogurt dollop to balance the harissa heat.
recipes.seasonal_note: Peak zucchini + fresh herbs = summer Mediterranean done right.
recipes.equipment: Skillet, sheet pan, small pot

recipes.name: Chicken Enchilada Verde Bowls

ingredients.name: Batch gochujang chicken (repurposed — toss with cumin + chili powder)

instructions: Warm shredded chicken in a skillet with salsa verde crema (tomatillo salsa + Greek yogurt + lime juice + cumin, blended).
Warm black beans and corn in the same skillet or microwave.
Build bowls: rice base, salsa verde chicken, black beans + corn, crushed tortilla chips, shredded cheese, cilantro.
Austin: pickled jalapeños + extra salsa verde. Cameron: sliced avocado + lighter salsa, extra cheese.
Squeeze lime over everything before eating.
recipes.batch_note: Uses batch chicken. Quick 10-min assembly on a weeknight.
recipes.cameron_note: + sliced avocado, lighter salsa verde, extra cheese for creaminess.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh corn just starting in season — use it if you can find it at the market.
recipes.equipment: Skillet

recipes.name: Thai Coconut Basil Shrimp
instructions: Heat 1 tsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Sear shrimp 1.5 min per side until pink; remove and set aside.
In the same pan: sauté garlic + ginger 30 sec. Add green curry paste, stir 30 sec until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk + fish sauce + brown sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Add bell pepper and snap peas; cook 3-4 min until crisp-tender.
Return shrimp to the pan. Add Thai basil leaves; stir until just wilted (30 sec).
Squeeze lime juice over everything. Austin: add sliced bird eye chili.
Serve over jasmine rice. Austin: 8 oz shrimp + larger rice portion. Cameron: 5 oz shrimp.
recipes.batch_note: Cook fresh Wednesday night — shrimp dishes are best day-of.
recipes.cameron_note: Use less curry paste (1 tbsp instead of 2) for her portion; no bird eye chili; extra coconut milk for creaminess.
recipes.seasonal_note: Last weeks of snap peas — enjoy them before summer fully arrives.
recipes.equipment: Large skillet or wok

recipes.name: Miso-Ginger Pork Stir-Fry with Snap Peas

ingredients.name: Mirin (or 1 tsp honey + 1 tsp rice vinegar)

instructions: Make miso-ginger sauce: whisk miso paste + soy sauce + mirin + sesame oil + grated ginger until smooth.
Slice pork tenderloin into 1/4-inch medallions against the grain.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until smoking. Sear pork 2 min per side until golden. Remove.
In the same pan: add snap peas + garlic. Stir-fry 2-3 min until peas are bright green and crisp-tender.
Return pork to pan. Pour in miso-ginger sauce. Toss everything 1 min until glazed and coated.
Serve over jasmine rice. Garnish with scallions + sesame seeds.
Austin: 7 oz pork, larger rice portion. Cameron: 5 oz pork.
recipes.batch_note: Cook fresh Thursday night — pork stir-fry is best day-of. Quick 22-min meal.
recipes.cameron_note: Smaller pork portion; slightly more rice. Miso-ginger is naturally mild — no adjustment needed.
recipes.seasonal_note: Final weeks of snap peas — make the most of them in this quick stir-fry.
recipes.equipment: Large skillet or wok

recipes.name: Lemon-Garlic Shrimp & Zucchini Linguine

ingredients.name: Linguine (from Sunday batch or cook fresh)

instructions: Cook linguine per package (or use Sunday batch — warm in pan with a splash of pasta water).
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil over high heat. Sear shrimp 1.5 min per side. Remove.
In the same pan: add remaining olive oil, sauté zucchini half-moons 3-4 min until lightly charred.
Add garlic + red pepper flakes. Cook 30 sec until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine or broth. Simmer 1 min.
Return shrimp. Add lemon juice + zest. Toss with cooked linguine.
Plate and top with parsley + grated Parmesan.
Austin: 7 oz shrimp. Cameron: 5 oz shrimp.
recipes.batch_note: Cook fresh Friday night. Can use Sunday batch linguine for speed.
recipes.cameron_note: Smaller shrimp portion; lighter on red pepper flakes. Extra lemon + Parmesan.
recipes.seasonal_note: Zucchini at its peak — the char on the half-moons is everything.
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, large pot (if cooking pasta fresh)

recipes.name: Smoked Pork Tenderloin with Cherry BBQ Glaze
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4 (Saturday dinner + Sunday lunch grain bowls)

ingredients.name: Coleslaw mix (no cabbage — use broccoli slaw)

instructions: FRIDAY NIGHT: dry brine pork tenderloins (see batch prep). Refrigerate overnight uncovered.
SATURDAY/SUNDAY: heat smoker to 250°F with cherry wood chips.
Place tenderloins on grate. Smoke 1.5-2 hours until internal temp reaches 145°F.
CHERRY BBQ GLAZE: while pork smokes, simmer pitted cherries + BBQ sauce + honey + red wine vinegar + smoked paprika + cayenne 15 min. Blend smooth or leave chunky.
Last 20 min of smoking: brush pork with cherry BBQ glaze every 10 min for a sticky lacquer.
Pull pork at 145°F internal. Rest 10 min tented with foil.
SIDES: grill or boil corn on the cob; toss broccoli slaw with apple cider vinegar + olive oil + salt for a quick slaw.
Slice pork. Serve with corn, slaw, and extra cherry BBQ glaze.
Reserve 1/3 of the pork for Sunday lunch grain bowls.
recipes.batch_note: Dry brine Friday night. Smoke Saturday or Sunday. Reserve leftover pork for Sunday grain bowl.
recipes.cameron_note: Smaller pork portion (5 oz vs 8 oz). Extra slaw. The cherry glaze is naturally sweet and mild — no adjustment needed.
recipes.seasonal_note: Cherries just hitting the market in Pittsburgh — the cherry BBQ glaze is the seasonal star.
recipes.equipment: Smoker, cherry wood chips

recipes.name: Greek Lemon Chicken & Potatoes with Tzatziki
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Toss halved baby potatoes with 2 tbsp olive oil, half the garlic, oregano, salt, pepper, and juice of 1 lemon. Spread in a single layer on a sheet pan.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt, pepper, oregano, remaining garlic. Nestle skin-side up on top of potatoes.
Drizzle with remaining olive oil. Pour chicken broth around the edges of the pan.
Roast 30-35 min until chicken skin is golden and crispy and internal temp hits 165°F. Add cherry tomato halves in the last 10 min.
Rest 5 min. Plate: potatoes, chicken (Austin: 2 thighs ~8 oz meat, Cameron: 1.5 thighs ~5 oz), roasted tomatoes.
Generous dollop of tzatziki. Fresh dill. Lemon wedges.
The pan juices are liquid gold — spoon them over everything.
recipes.batch_note: Cook fresh Sunday night. Uses batch tzatziki from Sunday prep.
recipes.cameron_note: Slightly smaller chicken portion. Extra potatoes and a very generous tzatziki dollop.
recipes.seasonal_note: Cherry tomatoes roasting in the pan add summer sweetness.
recipes.equipment: Large sheet pan

recipes.name: Antipasto Pasta Salad with Calabrian Chili Vinaigrette
recipes.serving_note: Serves 4 — adapted for macro targets by adding grilled chicken and adjusting portions

ingredients.name: Grilled chicken breast, diced (added for protein)
Salami or sopressata, sliced into strips
Marinated artichoke hearts, drained and chopped

instructions: Cook radiatori (or rotini) in well-salted water per package directions until al dente. Drain, rinse briefly with cold water to stop cooking, and toss with a drizzle of olive oil to prevent sticking.

MAKE VINAIGRETTE: Whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, pepperoncini brine, Dijon, mayo, grated garlic, Calabrian chili paste, oregano, grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper until emulsified. Taste and adjust — it should be punchy and a little spicy.
Grill or sear chicken breasts seasoned with salt, pepper, and a pinch of oregano. Rest 5 min, then dice into bite-sized pieces. (Or use batch-prepped chicken from Sunday cook.)
In a large bowl: combine cooled pasta, diced chicken, sliced salami, chopped artichoke hearts, olives, pepperoncini, cherry tomatoes, and mozzarella pearls.
Pour vinaigrette over everything and toss thoroughly. The pasta should be well-coated.
Top with torn basil, extra grated Parmesan, and cracked black pepper.
Serve immediately or refrigerate — this gets BETTER after a few hours as the flavors meld. Great for meal prep.
Austin: 6 oz chicken, full salami portion, extra Calabrian chili. Cameron: 4 oz chicken, full recipe, + 1/4 avocado on top.
recipes.batch_note: Excellent meal prep lunch — holds 4-5 days in the fridge and improves over time. Dress fully; the pasta absorbs the vinaigrette. Add a splash more vinaigrette day-of if needed.
recipes.cameron_note: + 1/4 avocado on top. Use 1 tsp Calabrian chili paste (milder end). The pepperoncini and olives give plenty of flavor without extra heat.
recipes.seasonal_note: Peak summer recipe — cherry tomatoes and fresh basil at their best. Great for hot days when you want a substantial cold meal.
recipes.equipment: Large pot, large mixing bowl, skillet or grill for chicken
recipes.source: Adapted from TikTok antipasto pasta salad recipe — Calabrian chili vinaigrette version. Added grilled chicken for protein targets.
